intro: Torna Hällestad is a village east of Lund in Skåne, and beside it lies the Trollskogen, the troll forest: a small beech wood where the trees grow twisted, their branches looping and kinking as if someone had wrung them. A reader sent us a photograph looking up into one of them in summer leaf. The wood is a nature reserve with free marked paths.

trees.name: The Twisted Beech of the Trollskogen

location.address: Trollskogsvägen, Gryteskog nature reserve (the Trollskogen), Torna Hällestad, Lund

trees.story:
People here once said the trolls had twisted them. The Trollskogen at Torna Hällestad, east of Lund, is a small forest of vresbokar, troll beeches, whose branches refuse to grow straight, and a reader sent us this one, photographed from beneath.

Lie back and look up, as they did. Instead of the clean grey columns of an ordinary beech wood, the limbs bend, loop back on themselves, kink sideways and set off again, black against a ceiling of fresh green leaves, so the whole crown looks like handwriting. Why these beeches grow like this is, in the county board's own word, a mystery: nobody is sure whether it is inherited or comes from the ground they stand on, and beechnuts from a twisted tree usually grow into straight ones.

The forest has been a nature reserve since 1959, with marked paths running among the trees. We do not yet know this tree's girth or age; if you measure it, tell us here and we will add your figures.

Come in summer, when the leaves are out, stand under it and follow one limb with your eyes from the trunk to its tip.
trees.how_to_recognise: In the Trollskogen beech wood: look up, and its dark limbs bend, loop and kink across the canopy instead of rising straight.

question_meta: A twisted beech in the Trollskogen at Torna Hällestad near Lund, sent by a reader: where it stands and how to find it.
question_answer: The Twisted Beech of the Trollskogen grows in the Gryteskog nature reserve at Torna Hällestad, east of Lund. Entry is free on the reserve's marked paths.
question_context: The Trollskogen, the troll forest, is the name people use for the Gryteskog nature reserve at Torna Hällestad, east of Lund in Skåne. It is a small beech wood, protected since 1959, where many of the beeches grow twisted: their branches bend, loop and kink instead of rising straight, and people once said trolls had wrung them. The county board calls the cause a mystery, unsure whether it is inherited or comes from the site, and notes that beechnuts from twisted trees usually grow into ordinary straight beeches. A reader sent us a photograph looking up into one of these trees in full summer leaf, the black limbs looping against a ceiling of fresh green, and that is the tree on our map. Marked paths run through the reserve, there is parking and a bus stop at its south-east corner, and entry is free. We do not yet know this tree's girth or age.

faq.q: Can I visit The Twisted Beech of the Trollskogen?
faq.a: Yes. It grows in the Gryteskog nature reserve, the Trollskogen, on public paths with free entry at all times.

faq.q: Why are the beeches in the Trollskogen twisted?
faq.a: Nobody is sure. The county board says it is unclear whether the twisting is inherited or comes from the site, and beechnuts from twisted trees usually grow into straight beeches.

faq.q: How do I get to the Trollskogen?
faq.a: It lies just outside Torna Hällestad, east of Lund. There is parking in the reserve's south-east corner, and the Gryteskog bus stop is right beside it.
